title: Using coding agents to push a 1994 console to its limits
author: izzy88izzy
selftext:
Hey everyone, I thought you might like this one. Coding agents have been helping people bring old consoles back to life lately, and I've loved seeing it on the Commodore, the Dreamcast and the PS2. I've been trying something similar on the PS1, in a different way: instead of one game at a time, I built some shared foundations first and put the games on top.

The project is called PSoXide. It's a toolkit for making games for the original PlayStation, written in Rust, and the idea behind it is to keep developing for the console as if it had never been retired. The SDK has no Sony code and doesn't rely on the BIOS. It talks to the graphics chip, the GTE geometry coprocessor, the sound chip, controllers, memory cards and the CD drive directly, which gives me control over every cycle of the frame. On top of it sits the engine behind my level editor, and the shooters share one more layer each: a BSP crate for Quake and a GoldSrc crate for Half-Life and Counter-Strike. Every game pins its own SDK version, so one change can't break all of them at once.

Agents do a lot of the work. My emulator and level editor both have MCP servers, so the agents can build a disc, boot it, replay recorded input and grab frames to see what the game does. None of that helps if the emulator is wrong, so I also check it against a real PS1: test discs print their results on screen as QR codes, I film them, and I fix the emulator wherever it doesn't match.

The video is a 12-minute walkthrough of where everything stands: ports of Half-Life, Hollow Knight, Ocarina of Time, Quake, Counter-Strike and Celeste, my own takes on Rocket League and Minecraft, a rebuilt WipEout, and Cortex Ignition, a Souls-like I'm working on. For each one I share a small trick it uses to fit on the hardware. If you're here for the AI side, that part starts at 10:06.

You can play some of it now. The free demo disc runs in your browser or on a real PS1, with Quake's shareware episode, NitroXide, VoXide, the Celeste collection and a Cortex Ignition tech demo. Half-Life builds from your own copy of the game.

None of it is finished, and I'm still learning a lot as I go. It's all free and open source if you want to poke around, and I'm happy to answer questions. I post all my games and updates on my YouTube channel, so that's the best place to follow along.



YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@bonnie-studios-dev](https://www.youtube.com/@bonnie-studios-dev)

Source and guides: [https://ebonura.github.io/PSoXide](https://ebonura.github.io/PSoXide)

Demo disc playable in your browser: [https://bonnie-studios.itch.io/psoxide](https://bonnie-studios.itch.io/psoxide)
